name: MinIO
description: Protects against destructive MinIO Client (mc) operations like bucket \ removal, object deletion, and admin operations.

destructive_patterns.name: mc-rb
destructive_patterns.description: mc rb removes a MinIO bucket.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing a MinIO bucket deletes the bucket and all objects within it. With \ --force, objects are deleted without confirmation. Applications referencing \ this bucket will fail immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - mc ls: List bucket contents first \ - mc cp --recursive: Backup to another location \ - Enable versioning or object locking before testing

destructive_patterns.name: mc-rm
destructive_patterns.description: mc rm deletes objects from MinIO.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting MinIO objects permanently removes data unless versioning is enabled. \ With --recursive, entire directory trees are deleted. With --force, no \ confirmation is requested.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - mc ls: Preview files to be deleted \ - mc cp: Backup objects before deletion \ - Enable bucket versioning for recovery

destructive_patterns.name: mc-admin-bucket-delete
destructive_patterns.description: mc admin bucket delete removes a bucket via admin API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The admin bucket delete command bypasses normal bucket deletion restrictions. \ This can remove buckets that are protected or non-empty. The operation is \ immediate and cannot be undone.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - mc admin info: Review cluster configuration \ - mc ls: Verify bucket contents first \ - Use standard mc rb for safer deletion

destructive_patterns.name: mc-mirror-remove
destructive_patterns.description: mc mirror --remove deletes destination objects not in source.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The --remove flag deletes objects from the destination that don't exist in \ the source. If source and destination are swapped, or source is empty, this \ can result in complete data loss at the destination.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - mc diff: Preview differences before mirroring \ - mc mirror without --remove: Only adds/updates \ - Backup destination before mirroring

destructive_patterns.name: mc-admin-user-remove
destructive_patterns.description: mc admin user remove/disable affects user access.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing or disabling a MinIO user revokes their access to all buckets and \ policies. Applications using this user's credentials will fail to authenticate. \ Service accounts created by this user may also be affected.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - mc admin user info: Review user permissions first \ - mc admin user disable: Disable instead of remove \ - Rotate credentials before removing user

destructive_patterns.name: mc-admin-policy-remove
destructive_patterns.description: mc admin policy remove/unset modifies access policies.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing or unsetting a policy affects all users and groups assigned to it. \ Users may unexpectedly lose access to buckets they need. Policy changes take \ effect immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - mc admin policy info: Review policy details \ - mc admin user list: Check who uses this policy \ - Create replacement policy before removing old one
